research_publication_context.purpose: Research-aware institutional context for Curly. Keep concise enough for normal prompt injection; use the source URLs for deeper retrieval or future updates.
research_narrative: Foundational yak research in husbandry, nutrition, reproduction, health and conservation.
Molecular and genetic research using markers, candidate genes and population characterisation.
Genomic research covering selection signatures, whole-genome variation, mitogenomics and transcriptomics.
Reproductive biotechnology including artificial insemination, semen cryopreservation, embryo transfer and FTAI.
Applied sustainability research spanning fodder, climate resilience, pastoral livelihoods and value addition.
Emerging digital research through AI, IoT, embedded systems, health monitoring, stress prediction and geo-fencing.

completed_project_themes: ethnopharmacology of medicinal plants used by yak rearers

genetics: NRCY reports association of 3-prime UTR Nramp1 polymorphism with brucellosis resistance in yak.
A PCR plus agarose-gel method was developed for Nramp1 genotyping.
TLR2 and TLR6 polymorphisms were characterised in yak.
A PCR-RFLP assay using SRY-related variation was developed to identify paternal origin in yak hybrids.
RAPD fingerprinting was developed for parentage/species-hybrid detection and differentiation among bovine species.
Growth hormone, growth hormone receptor and IGF-1 candidate-gene polymorphisms were studied; NRCY reports an association of IGF-1 polymorphism with birth weight.
nutrition: NRCY reports complete feed blocks using maize stover, concentrate and molasses as a winter-feed intervention.

The centre reports mineral supplementation experiments affecting puberty, body weight and reproductive efficiency; Curly should treat the reported historical values as study-specific, not universal yak benchmarks.
reproductive_biotechnology: NRCY annual reports document development of embryo and semen technologies, including IVF, embryo transfer and semen cryopreservation milestones.
The 2026 field FTAI demonstration in Sikkim involved 25 female yaks, 14 conceptions, a reported 56% conception rate and 10 healthy calves born on 29–30 June 2026.

faq.question: What is NRCY?
faq.answer: NRCY stands for ICAR–National Research Centre on Yak. It is a specialised ICAR research institute focused on yak research, conservation, breeding, health, nutrition, production and value addition.

faq.question: Who developed Curly?
faq.answer: Curly was developed by the Assam Don Bosco University technical team in collaboration with ICAR–National Research Centre on Yak.

faq.question: Where is NRCY located?
faq.answer: NRCY is located in Dirang, West Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh, India.

faq.question: Who is the Director of NRCY?
faq.answer: Dr. Mihir Sarkar is the current Director of ICAR–National Research Centre on Yak.

faq.question: Is NRCY part of ICAR?
faq.answer: Yes. ICAR–NRCY is a specialised research institute under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research.

faq.question: Is NRCY a university?
faq.answer: No. NRCY is a research institute under ICAR.

faq.question: Where is the NRCY yak farm?
faq.answer: NRCY has an experimental yak farm at Nyukmadung, approximately 31 kilometres from Dirang, at around 2,750 metres above mean sea level.

faq.question: What does NRCY research?
faq.answer: NRCY researches yak genetics, breeding, nutrition, health, reproduction, production, conservation, fibre, milk and other yak products.

faq.question: What is NRCY's recent AI project?
faq.answer: NRCY and Assam Don Bosco University developed an IoT-based smart system for yak health monitoring, stress prediction and geo-fencing.

faq.question: What is the recent breeding achievement of NRCY?
faq.answer: In 2026, NRCY demonstrated estrus synchronisation and Fixed-Time Artificial Insemination in yaks under field conditions in Sikkim.

faq.question: Does NRCY work outside Arunachal Pradesh?
faq.answer: Yes. NRCY conducts research, extension and technology-transfer activities in other Himalayan yak-rearing regions, including Sikkim and Ladakh.

faq.question: What is yak churpi?
faq.answer: Yak churpi is a traditional product made from yak milk. Arunachal Pradesh Yak Churpi has GI recognition, and NRCY has contributed to its promotion and value addition.
